task: RL-3 historical-analysis catastrophic-failure diagnostic (October/s863 primary case)
headline_finding: The catastrophic committed result does NOT reproduce with the current codebase and current checkpoint. It is explained, with high confidence, by a since-fixed simulation-engine concurrency bug (src/rl/env_fullstage_rl.py::_StageSignal) that was still present when the committed historical-analysis artifacts were generated, but is no longer present in the code now checked out at HEAD. This is a simulation-engine bug, not an RL-3 policy, reward, state-design, or generalisation failure.
central_evidence: Committed CSV (commit 406ecda) at October/s863: rl3_dqn picking_utilisation=0.1242 with 8 picking workers -- 0.1242 is within 0.6% of 1/8=0.125.

_StageSignal's own docstring (current code) explicitly documents a now-fixed prior bug whose exact symptom was 'picking utilisation stuck near 1/W regardless of backlog', caused by each worker calling its own event.reset() and orphaning the other W-1 workers' event references. The fix (single shared event owned by notify(), workers re-read signal.wait() fresh every iteration) is present and verified correctly applied at all three worker loops (picking/packing/dispatch) in the current file.

FIFO and urgent_first are UNAFFECTED in the same committed CSV (picking_utilisation~0.945, SLA~0.99) because they run through a structurally separate engine (run_simulation_multistage) that never uses _StageSignal -- explains why only rl3_dqn rows show the collapse.

Repeated reproduction attempts with the CURRENT code (rl_audit.py extended CLI, direct evaluate_monthly_capacity_cost calls, this diagnostic's own driver) on the byte-identical order data, the same checkpoint (verified stable SHA256 throughout), the same regime (s863), and the same service-time seed (133) ALL give good results (total_sla ~0.9915-0.9917), never the catastrophic ~0.0084.

The committed rl3_monthly_recommendations_summary.csv shows the SAME catastrophic RL-3 collapse (best_rl3_sla 0.0015-0.1291) uniformly across ALL 12 months -- including June/October/December, the exact 3 months RL-3 WAS trained on. A genuine policy/generalisation failure would be expected to spare at least the trained months; a systemic engine bug would not. This uniformity favours the engine-bug explanation over a policy-quality explanation.

Stress-tested the current code beyond October: December's large recommended regimes (s22_11_5 = 38 workers, s25_13_7 = 45 workers) both reproduce healthy RL-3 results (U=0.9922-0.9992, N=0.8540-0.9370) with the current engine -- rules out 'the fix only works at small worker counts'.

Fresh synthetic October/s863 probe, 3 new seeds never used anywhere in training or in the base data (90001/90002/90003): total_sla 0.9909-0.9921, stable and consistent with trajectories A (real historical) and B (training-file) -- Case B on the decision tree (fresh synthetic fine, and historical is ALSO fine once the engine bug is accounted for), not Case A (overfitting collapse) or Case C (seed instability).

Q-value diagnostics across A/B/C1/C2/C3 (21,779-21,996 real decision points each): no NaN/Inf, no queue-feature saturation (0.0% saturated in every trajectory), stable Q-value ranges (~104-142) and margins (median ~-0.07, mostly small) -- no sign of a degenerate or saturated policy at this regime.

root_cause_classification.primary: Class E -- implementation bug (simulation-engine concurrency bug in _StageSignal, since fixed in the code currently at HEAD)
root_cause_classification.secondary_latent_risk_not_currently_mani: Class B -- trajectory overfitting exposure. main_train_rl3.py exposes the agent to only 3 fixed order trajectories total (one per representative month: June/October/December; see training_methodology in october_historical_audit.json context and main_train_rl3.py::build_training_pool). This is a real, confirmed structural weakness in the training methodology, but the fresh-synthetic 3-seed probe and the Q-value stability evidence above show it is NOT currently causing a failure at October/s863 -- it remains a latent risk for future retraining/regimes, not an active explanation for the reported anomaly.
root_cause_classification.secondary_confidence: medium (methodology confirmed; consequence not currently observed)

evidence_against_primary_classification: The .pt checkpoint file is gitignored and has no git history, so its exact state at the moment the catastrophic historical analysis was actually run (vs. at the moment commit 406ecda was made, ~28h after the checkpoint's current mtime) cannot be proven from file metadata alone -- Class A (checkpoint version skew) cannot be fully excluded, only judged unlikely given the mtime evidence.

The 'older, buggy _StageSignal' version was never captured in a separate commit -- its existence is inferred from the current code's own docstring description plus the near-exact 1/W numerical match, not from a literal diff against a prior committed version. This is strong circumstantial evidence, not a direct before/after code comparison.

Only 2 of the 12 months (October across several regimes, December at 2 large regimes) were actually re-run end-to-end with the current code as part of this diagnostic; the other 9 months' committed catastrophic rows were not individually re-reproduced (though the uniform 1/W-style collapse pattern and the shared-engine argument apply equally to all of them).
